page_title: Why Good Developers are Promoted into Unhappiness | Rob Walling

sources.entry: Why Good Developers are Promoted into Unhappiness, Rob Walling. Or why management might not be for you.

summary.title: Why Good Developers are Promoted into Unhappiness
summary.one_liner: Good developers are often promoted into management roles that pull them away from coding, and the author argues companies should promote managers-in-waiting instead of their best programmers.
keywords: why good engineers become bad managers
takeaways: Top developers are often promoted into management, where they write little or no code and become unhappy.
The problem is not promotion itself but promoting big producers instead of people with management skills.
Developers often accept management for prestige, money, pressure, or to avoid stirring the pot.
Managers who want to code should move back into hands-on work sooner rather than later, before burnout sets in.
Companies should promote developers who demonstrate management skills instead of their top technical performers.
summary.summary: Rob Walling describes his own path from a management training program to software development, then to supervising 10 developers at a city government, and back to consulting as a coder. He notes that several other developers reported nearly identical experiences. The essay argues that promoting top developers wastes their technical contribution and frustrates them, using a baseball analogy about a star player made manager. It closes by urging managers who miss coding to return to it now and suggesting companies promote people who show real management skills.
